context.body: God deals well with the midwives, gives them families, and the people continue to multiply.
context.label: Named outcomes

observations.body: The new king does not know Joseph and describes Israel as more numerous and mightier than his own people.
observations.label: A new king

observations.body: Taskmasters afflict Israel, yet the passage says that greater affliction is followed by greater multiplication and spreading.
observations.label: Pressure and growth

observations.body: Shiphrah and Puah receive the king’s command, fear God, and keep the boys alive.
observations.label: The midwives

observations.body: A command given to two midwives becomes a command to all Pharaoh’s people to cast every son into the river.
observations.label: The command widens

payload.posture: Read the escalation one step at a time, keeping each speaker, command, and response distinct.
payload.tension: The policies intended to limit Israel intensify while the passage repeatedly reports Israel multiplying.
payload.title: Fear becomes policy
